medium.clue: Furry companion that purrs on your lap.

hard.clue: It always lands on its feet.

rule1_bad: For WOULD, answering "I would if it rained tomorrow" — WOULD itself must never appear in the clue text, even as part of a sentence.
rule2_bad: "third person singular present tense of a verb" for a verb form.
for FAIRIES, "Plural of 'fairy'" — naming the grammatical operation (pluralization) and repeating the singular form is still a label, not a clue.
rule2_good: for FAIRIES, "Magical beings from folk tales." (in the correct plural form, per rule 4).
rule3_bad: For TEE, "Word that starts with T and ends with EE." — that describes how the word is written, not what it means.
rule4_bad: For WAS — first/third person singular PAST of "to be" — answering "We celebrated the end of exams" or "They were no longer the same after the trip": both describe a past state but neither is singular ("we"/"they" need WERE, not WAS), so neither fits.

For SUNG — past PARTICIPLE of "sing" (used with a helper verb, e.g. "has sung") — answering "The bird sang at dawn" (that's the simple past, SANG): wrong form — the clue must itself imply a helper verb, e.g. "What a choir has done by the end of the concert", not a stand-alone past-tense action.

For WILL — future modal auxiliary — answering "What lies hide" (a timeless present-tense statement): the clue itself must carry future framing (e.g. "What tomorrow holds") to match a word that specifically marks futurity, not a generic present-tense description.

For MICE — PLURAL (irregular: mouse → mice) — answering "A small rodent": that describes ONE mouse, not several — the clue must itself refer to more than one to fit a plural word, e.g. "Small rodents said to play while the cat's away."
rule4_good: RUNS (he/she/it, present) : What a marathon competitor does each morning before work
WALKED (past, regular) : What tourists did along the beach at sunset yesterday
RAN (past, irregular) : What she did to catch the last train
WRITTEN (past participle, used with has/have/had) : What a novel is, once an author has finished it
SPOKEN (past participle, used with has/have/had) : What words are, once someone has said them aloud
SINGING (present participle) : What a choir is doing during rehearsal right now
TEACHES (he/she/it, present) : What a professor does every semester
WENT (past, irregular) : What the whole family did on vacation last summer
EATEN (past participle, used with has/have/had) : What a meal is, once every last bite has been finished
WOULD (conditional modal) : What you'd say to describe a hypothetical outcome, given the chance
COULD (past/conditional modal of ability) : What she said about her chances of winning, before the results came in
SHOULD (modal of obligation/advice) : What a doctor tells a patient about taking their medicine
MICE (plural, irregular: mouse → mice) : Small rodents said to play while the cat's away
GEESE (plural, irregular: goose → geese) : Migratory birds that fly together in a V formation
CHILDREN (plural, irregular: child → children) : Young people who eventually stop believing department-store Santas are real
TEETH (plural, irregular: tooth → teeth) : What a dentist examines, one by one, during a checkup
FEET (plural, irregular: foot → feet) : What shoes are meant to protect, both of them
WOMEN (plural, irregular: woman → women) : Attendees at a conference held specifically for female entrepreneurs
WAS (I/he/she/it, past) : One traveler's state, right after the long journey
WERE (we/you/they, past) : Several travelers' state, right after the long journey
rule5_bad: For MIGHT — modal verb expressing possibility ("it might rain") — answering "Purchased at the corner shop": that has no connection at all to the meaning of possibility, it is simply a different, unrelated idea.
